summary: Sky Motion Explorer furthers what other software using SPHEREx hasn't done yet: Allowing for both the viewing of known data and the evaluation of potential discoveries using that data. With a dataset of hundreds of millions of files captured by SPHEREx, Sky Motion Explorer filters through only what is relevant and displays the data. Along with displaying the data, multiple tools are at your disposal, allowing researchers, astronomers, and curious individuals to find new insights about space: A new planetary object, the history of our universe, or even life on a faraway planet.
details:
Sky Motion Explorer allows users to view relevant data on space by just entering the target name or the relevant Right Ascension and Declination data. After entering the data, the software does all the work: Looks through the historical IRSA data by NASA using Astropy to find the relevant SPHEREx data corresponding to the object you're looking for. If found, the software works together with the frontend and the backend to display the data, accessed in the corresponding FITS file, across the tens to hundreds of potentially found data related to the object in question. After collection, multiple data visualization tools can be used by the user to make new observations on the data.

This project benefits from having all of the relevant data be collected and displayed in a uniform way to the user. No irrelevant object data is displayed the user, meaning that the user doesn't have to dig through hundreds of millions of files just to find the object they are looking for. Our software does it all for them. This also ties into the impact of our software: With everyone being in one place, astronomers and researchers can just as easily create new observations that they would otherwise have to go search for on their own. This cuts the time for research by a lot, meaning that researchers can find life on other planets in the near future.

Tools and Libraries we used: Astropy, s3fs, git
Coding languages: Python, HTML, CSS, Javascript

Software: VSCode, Github

Our project's creativity comes in how our data is being visualized. This also ties into the thought process our team had when making the project. It isn't enough to just display the relevant data, we also want the data to look good and be usable for the researcher who is using our software. What good is software that has all the data necessary, but is hard to look at? We fixed this problem by allowing users to customize the display of the 49x49 frame in multiple ways. We allow the HUD to be hidden and displayed for cleaner screenshots. Users can change how the pixels look by changing the colormap and how the intensity is shown. We allow for visualization of not just a default 49x49, but even a smaller or bigger FOV. We also allowed for highlighted target points to be displayed in different opacities and shapes.
